title: mysql performance tuning
linkedin:
Measure before you touch anything.

Turn on the slow query log to catch your slowest statements, run `EXPLAIN` to see why they're slow, and add an index on the columns you filter, join, and sort on. Size the InnoDB buffer pool so your hot data and indexes live in RAM, pool your connections so MySQL isn't buried under them, and resize the server only when it's genuinely maxed. In that order.

Read the full guide: https://www.kloudbean.com/blog/mysql-performance-tuning/
